items.name: Ymir Agathodaemon Hammer
items.description: Chapter IV: The Agathodaemon, destructive as always, crumbled the tops of the coiled stone into earth and soil. He layed this soil over Vritra's wings, forming the ground as we know it. The Agathodaemon's hammer can crush the Ward of your opponent.

items.name: Ymir Beithir's Staff
items.description: Aside: As Illuyanka's walls were raised, protection for this new land was needed. Beithir, with the breath of lightning and claws of toxin, replicated itself indefinitely. An army of Dragons was created in an instant.

items.name: Ymir Brilliant Feathers
items.description: Chapter IX: Quetzalcoatl flew high, shedding her feathers in the air. As the sun melted her feathers, they filled the craters Bashe left behind, forming our lakes and rivers. Her remaining feathers form this scythe, and it will better align you with your faction's might.

items.name: Ymir Cliffside Cuirass
items.description: Chapter VI: Illuyanka then raised walls of stone to frame this new land from the raging seas and winds. The cliffs and shores can be seen from afar, and her mighty armor will surely make one feel as they are made of the cliffs themselves. It will occasionally protect you from hits that take 100% of your maximum HP.
traits: Damage Protect: 100% Max HP Damage (25% chance)

items.name: Ymir Coiled Shield
items.description: Chapter I: These lands were created by the Great Dragons: 8 deities formed by the wants and wishes of humankind. Lotan was the first to mend the earth, coiling rock from the planet's core to create the foundation of life. Her shield will greatly decrease the damage taken when defending in battle.

items.name: Ymir Staff of Zaltys
items.description: Chapter V: Zaltys never did like the Agathodaemon, but understood that she needed the soil for life. Zaltys laid seed to the soil, sprouting the foliage that lets us breath our air. Her staff represents life, and will allow you to recover HP each turn in battle.

items.name: Ymir Vritra Charm
items.description: Chapter III: Vritra was next to forge these lands, laying her immutable wings upon the coiled rock. This formed a basin of strength for life to grow atop the molten core of this planet. Her charm may occasionally protect you from status effects while granting immunity to Paralyze, Stun, and Petrification.

items.name: Ymir World Eater
items.description: Chapter VIII: Bashe, the World Eater -- hungry as ever -- drove his mouth downwards, piercing the foundation of the Agathodaemon. His broadsword is filled with craters as well, making it well suitable for adornment.

dungeons.name: Dungeon
dungeons.description: A standard dungeon. Fight monsters through a series of floors for unique rewards.

dungeons.name: Goblin Fortress
dungeons.description: A dungeon filled with Goblin type enemies. This dungeon rewards extra gold.

dungeons.name: Mystic Cave
dungeons.description: A dungeon filled with magical type enemies. This dungeon rewards extra orns.

dungeons.name: Beast Den
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon filled with beast type enemies. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra orns.

dungeons.name: Dragon Roost
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon filled with dragon type enemies. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra orns.

dungeons.name: Underworld Portal
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon filled with enemies of the Underworld. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra items.

dungeons.name: Chaos Portal
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon filled with enemies of all weather conditions. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra items.

dungeons.name: Battlegrounds
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon where Lyonesse and Nothren clash. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra items.

dungeons.name: Valley of the Gods
dungeons.description: A Battle Dungeon of the most powerful foes. This Battle Dungeon rewards extra items, gold, and orns.

dungeons.name: Final Bloom Lair
dungeons.description: Raid the Final Bloom's jungle lair to earn the Melody of the Amazon.

dungeons.name: Seedhusk of Yggdrasil
dungeons.description: Fight off Nothren defenders to break the Seedhusk, earning a Seed of Yggdrasil.

dungeons.name: Darkrift Dungeon
dungeons.description: Encounter Fallen Judge Zagreus and his Darkrift army.

dungeons.name: Dullahan Den
dungeons.description: Defeat all the Headless minions of The Dullahan to earn a Haunted Calling Bell.

dungeons.name: Giant Pumpkin
dungeons.description: Trick or treat or treat or trick.

buildings.name: Shop
buildings.description: Build your own shop in this area. Shops rotate a stock of items frequently.

buildings.name: Bestiary
buildings.description: Build your own bestiary in this area. Bestiaries allow the player to hire a follower.

buildings.name: Blacksmith
buildings.description: Build your own blacksmith in this area. Blacksmiths are used to upgrade weapons and equipment.

buildings.name: Grand Market
buildings.description: Build a large marketplace in this area. Marketplaces rotate a huge stock of items and can save one's town many a built shop.

buildings.name: Keep
buildings.description: Build a keep in your origin town. Keeps can be used to store gold and followers.

buildings.name: Fortress
buildings.description: Upgrade your Keep to a Fortress to improve its storage limits and give access to an Alchemist and Dungeon.

buildings.name: Castle
buildings.description: Upgrade your Fortress to a Castle to improve its storage limits and give access to a Demonforge and Coliseum.

buildings.name: Town Hall
buildings.description: Build a town hall in your origin town. You will need a town hall to start attracting villagers.

buildings.name: Citadel
buildings.description: Build a citadel to collect offerings from your villagers. The higher the population and morale, the more likely you are to receive offerings.

buildings.name: Residence
buildings.description: Build residences to increase the population of your origin town.

buildings.name: Herbalist
buildings.description: Hire a herbalist in this area. Herbalists can craft various potions.

buildings.name: Oracle Temple
buildings.description: Hire a skilled Elysian Oracle in this area. Oracles can occasionaly grant one Diluted Mnemonics. Additionally, they can transform unused Amities in to Diluted Mnemonics.

buildings.name: Appraiser
buildings.description: Hire an item appraiser in this area. Appraisers can show you the rating of recently acquired items.

buildings.name: Fishing Hut
buildings.description: Build a fishing hut in this area. Anglers can trade in fish and coral for unique items here.

buildings.name: Spelunking Guild
buildings.description: Build the Guild Hall of the Spelunking Guild. Dungeon divers can earn Proofs of Spelunking from Dungeons and exchange them for unique items here.

buildings.name: Monumental Guild
buildings.description: Build the Guild Hall of the Monumental Guild. The Monumental Guild rewards you for participating in in-game events.

buildings.name: Titan Workshop
buildings.description: Construct a Workshop of the Titans in this area. Titan Workshops can be used to construct Towers of Olympia. Additionally, Titans weapons and classes can be unlocked here.

buildings.name: Wayvessel
buildings.description: Build a Wayvessel. Wayvessels may be used to travel freely between party members' origin towns. Additionally, they can be used to freely return to your Origin Town when you are away.

buildings.name: Traveler's Guild Hall
buildings.description: Build a Travelers's Guild Hall to compete in Guild Trials.

buildings.name: Conqueror's Guild Hall
buildings.description: Build a Conqueror's Guild Hall to receive rewards for Settlements that you conquer.

buildings.name: Blades of Finesse
buildings.description: Build the Guild Hall of the Blades of Finesse to compete in live PvP against other players.

buildings.name: Circle of Anguish
buildings.description: For those looking for a additional gameplay challenge, join the Circle of Anguish.

buildings.name: Altar of Ascension
buildings.description: Build an Altar of Ascension to offer your earnings to the Gods in return for power.

buildings.name: Outpost
buildings.description: An extension of your Keep that allows follower and item management from afar.

buildings.name: Jeweller
buildings.description: Hire a jeweller in this area. Jewellers can sell adornments and adorn weapons or armor.

buildings.name: Refinery
buildings.description: Build a refinery in this area. Refineries can be used to occasionally harvest materials.

buildings.name: Inn
buildings.description: Visit Inns to take jobs from their job boards. You may also receive local information at the Tavern.

buildings.name: Alchemist
buildings.description: Visit this forge to Masterforge your equipment, bringing items from level 10 to 11. You may also adorn items here.

buildings.name: Demonforge
buildings.description: Visit this forge to Demonforge your equipment, bringing items from level 11 to 12.

buildings.name: Bazaar
buildings.description: Find the rare bazaar to purchase an assortment of unique items.

buildings.name: Coliseum
buildings.description: For an ultimate challenge, fight against a series of your peers in the Coliseum.

topics.name: Character movement
body: Orna: The GPS RPG is a location-based game that uses your real-world location to progress your character in an in-game world.
Moving your in-game character position is done by moving around in the real world, with your device in hand.

topics.name: Battle
body: As your progress through the game, you will spend a good amount of time in battle against monsters, bosses, and optionally other players.
When in battle, battle members take turns attacking, using Skills or Spells, defending, or using items.
Battles end when the HP of either side reaches 0.

If an encounter proves too difficult for you, you can always run away by holding down the "Flee" button in battle, when available. In most cases, you will be able to fight the same encounter again after a short period of time.

topics.name: Currency
body: There are two major currencies found in your travels: Gold and Orns.
Gold is the primary currency used in shops. You can exchange Gold for items, followers, item upgrades, and more.
Orns are used to progress your character. You can exchange Orns for class upgrades, high level followers, specializations, and more.
Orns are earned by completing Quests, earning Achievements, participating in Raids or Dungeons, and more.

topics.name: Codex
body: The Codex is your primary source of information in the game.
In addition to the tutorials you are viewing now, information that you learn about monsters, bosses, followers, and raids will be stored in the Codex.
You can reference the Codex while in battle to reference information and weaknesses that you have learned about your opponent.

topics.name: Skills and Spells
body: Abilities available in combat are considered one of two categories: Skills and Spells.
When in your Skills menu, Skills are denoted by a sword icon.
The damage dealt by Skills is determined by your Attack stat. Damage will be reduced depending on your opponent's Defense stat.
When in your Spells menu, Spells are denoted by a staff icon.
The damage dealt by Spells is determined by your Magic stat. Damage will be reduced depending on your opponent's Resistance stat.

topics.name: Elemental weaknesses
body: There are four primary elements found in the game: Fire, Water, Earth, and Lightning.
Enemies found can be weak to, immune to, or have resistance to any element.
To maximize your damage against enemies, prioritize Skills or Spells of an element that your opponent is weak to.
There are five secondary elements found in the game: Physical, Dragon, Arcane, Dark, and Holy.

topics.name: Quests
body: Quests from many places can be found and accepted in your travels.
Quests will be one of the best sources of Orns and experience points for your character.
Additionally, completing daily quests will grant you a number of bonuses that boost experience point gain or chances to find rare items for the day.

topics.name: Blacksmiths
body: Upgrading your equipment is essential to ensure you can take on more powerful foes.
Blacksmiths will upgrade pieces of your equipment to increase their stats. Each upgrade will cost gold, orns, and materials. The price to upgrade increases each time, per item.
While a piece of equipment is being upgraded, it cannot be used by your character.
When your piece of equipment is done being upgraded, it can be retrieved from any Blacksmith found in the world.

topics.name: Tiers & player level
body: When your character has received sufficient experience points, it will automatically level up. Upon levelling up, your characters stats will increase and, depending on your character class, it may learn new Spells or Skills to use in battle.
Content in the game is divided into tiers. Tiers occur every 25 levels.
Upon reaching a new tier, more powerful monsters, bosses, and equipment will become available to you.
Tier 1: Levels 1 - 24
Tier 2: Levels 25 - 49
Tier 3: Levels 50 - 74
Tier 4: Levels 75 - 99
Tier 5: Levels 100 - 124
Tier 6: Levels 125 - 149
Tier 7: Levels 150 - 174
Tier 8: Levels 175 - 199
Tier 9: Levels 200 - 224
Tier 10: Levels 225 - 249
Tier 11: Level 250

topics.name: Item drops & quality
body: Nearly all enemies in the game have a set list of items that they can drop when defeated. The list of dropped items can be found here in the Codex, upon being discovered.
Weapons, Armor, and Accessories dropped by enemies can be of a quality.
Items can be found in the following qualities: Broken, Poor, Standard, Superior, Famed, Legendary, and finally the rarest of all, Ornate.

Broken and Poor items will have reduced stats, passive effects, and value. While they're most often sold, you may have one that is worth upgrading at the Blacksmith, or otherwise of use to your character. They have a quality rating of under 50.
Standard items have normal stats and value. They have a quality rating of 50.
Superior, Famed, and Legendary items have slightly greater stats or passive effects. They have a quality rating between 70 and 85.
Ornate items are the most rare, but can have up to double the stats or passive effects. They have a quality rating between 85 and 100.
Items found have a 1/200 chance to be Ornate.

topics.name: Resource & material collection
body: Materials like Wood, Stone, Leather, and Hide can be found from many sources throughout your travels.
When travelling throughout the world, you will find resource nodes that can be interacted with to receive materials.
Many enemies will also drop materials when defeated. These materials can be searched for in the Codex.
Shops, Bazaars, and Guild Shops will hold rotating stocks of materials.
Dismantling equipment that has been found or bought from shops will also yield materials.

topics.name: Character parties
body: Players can form and join Parties with other players. After being added as an Ally, players can send Party Invites to each other.
When players are in a Party, they will share all experience points earned in battle with that Party.
Party members who are currently inactive will not have experience points shared with them.
Party members who are more than 25 levels apart will not share experience with one another.
Party members can join one another in battle, enter Dungeons together, and battle Raids together.

topics.name: Character classes
body: A player's class determines what Spells or Skills they will learn as they level up.
Additionally, the player's class will determine what Passive Abilities are available to them. Passive Abilities are always active and do not need to be cast or used.
When a class's Spell or Skill is learned, it can then additionally be used in battle by any other class chosen by the player.
A player's base stats will also be determined by their class and current level.

topics.name: Specializations
body: In addition to class, players can also choose a Specialization.
Specializations augment a player's current class by adding additional Passive Abilities, Spells or Skills, and stats.
Spells or Skills learned from a Specialization can no longer be used if the player chooses a new Specialization, but can be used again if switching back to the previous Specialization.

topics.name: Origin Town
body: Your Origin Town is your home base in the game. It is where you will start your journey and where you will return to after your travels.
You can build many useful buildings while in your Origin Town.
When in your Origin Town, you will receive a stat bonus.
Other players can visit your Origin Town by building and activating their Wayvessel to travel to yours.

topics.name: Followers
body: A Follower is a companion in your travels. They can join you in battle and provide assistance via buffs, debuffs, or offensive Skills or Spells.
Both your Follower and your opponent's Follower cannot be damaged in battle.
Followers can be taken with you from any Bestiary building found in the world or build. Followers will cost Gold to take with you. The most powerful Followers will cost Orns.
Your Follower storage can be used to store all Followers that you have taken with you. They can be retrieved at any time.

topics.name: Factions
body: All players in the game eventually align to a Faction. A Faction represents an alignment with one of the primary elements: Fire, Water, Earth, or Lightning.
Factions are not for online play. They provide bonuses when using Skills or Spells of the same element as your Faction.
Additionally, they may have some secondary effects in different gameplay modes.
Players are first prompted to join a faction at level 10.
If a player chooses not to align to a faction immediately, they will be prompted again upon each level up, or after closing and restarting the game.

topics.name: Kingdoms
body: Kingdoms are groups of players that have joined together to form a community.
Many special activities are available to Kingdoms, including Kingdom Raids, Kingdom Wars, and more.
Each Kingdom has a preferred level of player engagement. Always make sure you are joining a Kingdom that aligns with your playstyle the best.
Kingdoms that require a higher level of engagement will generally have higher requirements to join. Additionally, they may remove players that do not meet their engagement requirements.
Joining a helpful Kingdom and participating in Kingdom activities is one of the best ways to progress your character quickly.

topics.name: Adornments
body: Adornments are small items that you may find in your travels. They can be added to weapons or pieces of armor at an Alchemist or Jeweller building.
Adornments can add a variety special effects to your equipment. Additionally, they often come with stats that are added to your equipment.
Pieces of equipment must be upgraded at a Blacksmith to unlock their Adornment slots.

topics.name: Weather effects
body: Weather effects can occur in any area, at any time of day. Their patterns repeat within a longer period of time.
When a weather effect is occurring in your area, you will see a weather icon at the top of your screen. This weather effect may bring in monsters that are unique to that weather effect.
But be careful. Weather effects can cause you or your opponent to start battles with active debuffs.

topics.name: Achievements
body: Achivements are earned by completing various targets in the game. They can be viewed from the Achievements menu.
These targets may include defeating a certain number of monsters, defeating a certain number of bosses, or defeating a certain number of players in PvP.
Earning Achievements is a great source of orns.

topics.name: Game Events
body: Every month, the game features a new primary event. This event generally brings new items, monsters, bosses, raids, and quests to the game for a limited-time.
Additionally, each month features secondary events. These are the primary events of other months, but run for a shorter amount of time.
Bonus events also occur a few times a month. These events generally feature increased experience, Orns, and Gold for a limited-time.

topics.name: Follower action rates
body: Followers all have action rates for certain types of actions (Buffs, debuffs, offense Skills, etc.).
In addition, they may have a chance to protect you from an attack in battle.
These rates can be viewed in the Codex.
Equipment can be found that will increase the action rates of your Follower.

Additionally, Skills known as "Calls" can be used to increase the action rates of your Follower when in-battle. Calls are learned by higher tier classes. Calls are only truly effective when used by a Valhallan class.

topics.name: Equipment sets
body: Equipment sets can be utilized to save a current combination of equipped items and Skills or Spells.
Players are granted 4 equipment sets per loadout, per class.
Additional equipment sets can be purchased from the Runeshop.

topics.name: Charged passives & abilities
body: Charged Passive Abilities such as Dragon Slayer, Eternal Light, and Crest of Avalon will have its charge determined by the last 48 hours of playtime.
Enemies defeated or playtime from 49+ hours ago will not contibute to your current active percentage of these abilities.
This same timeline applies to charged Skills or Spells, such as Dragon's Vengeance, Nekrosis, and Sorrow.

topics.name: Amities
body: Amities are found when performing Shattered Memory Hunts.

Amities are useful pieces of equipment that can be equipped to your characterin the Amity slot. They provide unique Passive Abilities to your character, but also provide a negative malus to your character.
An Amity is determined by memories found when performing a Shattered Memory Hunt, as well as your answers to any questions that may have been asked.

topics.name: Summons
body: Some classes can summon monsters into battle with them, known as Summons.
These Summons do not act any differently than their monster counterparts.
Monsters summoned into battle will not be able to contribute to the summoning player's Codex, so use summons carefully when Codexing enemies.

topics.name: Hybrid Skills
body: Some Skills or Spells are hybrid and will use a combination of both your Attack and Magic stats.
Subsequently, your opponent will require both adequate Defense and Resistance to reduce the Skill or Spell's damage.

topics.name: Godforging
body: Godforging is a process that allows players to upgrade their equipment to the highest possible level.
When defeating an enemy that is denoted with a yellow aura, any Demonforged equipment that you have equipped will have the chance to be immediately upgraded to Godforged.
Only one piece of equipment can be Godforged per battle.

topics.name: Traveler's Guild
body: The Traveler's Guild is the first Guild you will encounter. It is a Guild that rewards you for daily and weekly step goals.
When walking on a daily basis, you will earn Proofs of Distance. These can be used to purchase items from the Guild Shop.
Additionally, you can charge Traveler Aspects to earn monster allies or items.

When contributing daily steps towards the Traveler's Guild, "Traveler's Intuition" will reward you with materials, gold, orns or Proofs of Distance as you travel by foot. These rewards become visible on the map as you walk.
Build the Traveler's Guild Hall in your Origin Town to use your Monster Manifests in Guild Trials.

topics.name: The Spelunking Guild
body: The Spelunking Guild is a Guild that rewards players for mining Deepshards in Exploration Dungeons.
This Guild can be accessed after building a Spelunking Guild Hall in your Origin Town.

topics.name: The Monumental Guild
body: The Monumental Guild rewards players for participating in limited-time in-game events, specifically through Monument buildings found in the world.
Additionally, Proof of Felling earned by defeating Raids can be spent here.
This Guild Hall can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: The Conqueror's Guild
body: The Conqueror's Guild is a competitive Guild that rewards players for claiming Settlements as their own.
Complete with both NPCs and other players to hold control over Settlements, earning you daily rewards at the Conqueror's Guild Hall.

topics.name: The Seer's Guild
body: The Seer's Guild is a Guild that rewards players for completing Memory Hunts.
This Guild can be accessed from any Oracle Temple.

topics.name: The Angler's Guild
body: The Angler's Guild is a Guild that rewards players for fishing.
This Guild can be accessed from a Fishing Hut.

topics.name: The Blades of Finesse
body: The Blades of Finesse is a Guild that allows players to challenge other players in realtime PvP battles.
This Guild Hall can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: The Circle of Anguish
body: For players looking for an extra challenge, the Circle of Anguish allows players to increase game difficulty for extra rewards.
This Guild Hall can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: The Titanfelled
body: The Titanfelled Guild is a Guild that rewards players for completed Towers of Olympia.
This Guild can be accessed from a Titan Workshop.

topics.name: Battle Dungeons
body: Battle Dungeons can be found throughout the world and can be played solo or with a party. Additionally, they are visible on the map when traveling through a Wayvessel.
In Battle Dungeons, players fight through series of floors containing monster encounters.

When a Battle Dungeon is completed, players will be rewarded with a number of items, Gold, materials, and Orns. Additionally, completing Battle Dungeons will grant the chance to receive any item that was previously earned through a Story Quest.
Skeleton Keys are required to enter any dungeon.
Battle Dungeons can also be found in a variety of themes: Dragon Roosts, Beast Dens, and more. These themes may have additional rewards and bonuses.

topics.name: Exploration Dungeons
body: Exploration Dungeons can be found throughout the world and can be played solo or with a party. Additionally, they are visible on the map when traveling through a Wayvessel.
In Exploration Dungeons, players progress through a series of floors containing monster encounters and resource nodes to mine.
Refining resources within Exploration Dungeons will yield Deepshards, a currency used in the Spelunking Guild.

When the final boss of an Exploration Dungeon is defeated, players will be rewarded with a number of items, Gold, materials, and Orns. Additionally, completing Exploration Dungeons will grant the chance to receive any item that was previously earned through a Story Quest.
Skeleton Keys are required to enter any dungeon.
Exploration Dungeons are found in one of two themes: the Goblin Fortress and the Mystic Cave.

topics.name: Memory Hunting
body: Memory Hunts can be started by using the Diluted Mnemonic consumable item. Diluted Mnemonics can be acquired at an Oracle Temple, through daily rewards, or various Guild Shops.
When a Memory Hunt is started, players will be tasked with finding a number of Shattered Memories in the world. These can be found by exploring the world.

If a Shattered Memory is out of reach, exploring the world in another direction should lead to a different Shattered Memory. There is generally always more than one Shattered Memory available to be found.
Memory Hunts end after five Shattered Memories have been found. When a Memory Hunt is complete, the player is rewarded with an equippable Amity.

topics.name: Kingdom Raids
body: Kingdoms can summon powerful Raid bosses by spending earned Kingdom Orns.
Some Kingdom Raids will require a minimum Kingdom level, earned by competing in Kingdom Wars or completing Kingdom Quests.
Kingdom Officers can set a limit on how much damage a single player can constribute to Kingdom Raids, ensuring that all Kingdom members have a chance to participate.
Upon joining a new Kingdom, players must wait 24 hours before they can participate in Kingdom Raids. This ensures players cannot leave and join Kingdoms to farm their Raids.
When a Raid is completed, rewards will be given to all players who had contributed damage to the Raid. These rewards may come instantly or after a short period of time.

topics.name: World Raids
body: World Raids can be summoned to your nearby area by using a Summoning Scroll.
World Raids can be completed solo or with a Party.
When completing World Raids with a Party, all players that haven't fallen in battle will be eligible for rewards.
When a Raid is completed, rewards will be given to all players who had contributed damage to the Raid. These rewards may come instantly or after a short period of time.

topics.name: Monuments
body: The Great Monuments are traversable dungeons that can be found in the world.
They are a great place to encounter monsters pertaining to currently active in-game events, or monsters that may not easily be found elsewhere in the world.
Completing a Great Monument will give a passive effect that will last for 2 hours. This passive effect will depend on the God that the Monument is dedicated to.
Monuments are aligned to Factions and are free to enter for players aligned to the same Faction. Otherwise, it will cost a Skeleton Key to enter.
Monuments are single player experiences and cannot be seen through Wayvessels.
Monuments reset and change locations once a week. This reset occurs on Monday at 00:00 UTC.

topics.name: Towers of Olympia
body: The Towers of Olympia are traversable dungeons that can be found in the world.
Ascending the Towers of Olympia can yield a variety of endgame rewards.
Their floor counts change every few hours. Towers with higher floor counts will be more difficult and take longer to complete, but will yield additional rewards at higher floors.
A Tower Key is required to enter a Tower of Olympia.
Towers of Olympia are single player experiences and cannot be seen through Wayvessels.
Towers of Olympia reset and change locations once a week. This reset occurs on Monday at 00:00 UTC.

topics.name: Shop
body: The humble Shop is the simplest of buildings. It allows you to purchase items with Gold.
Shops restock their inventory every few days.
This building can be found in the world or built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Blacksmith
body: Visit a Blacksmith to upgrade your equipment. Upgrading your equipment will increase its stats. When an item is finished upgrading, it can be retrieved from any blacksmith.
Additionally, a Blacksmith can remove Adornments from your equipment.
This building can be found in the world or built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Bestiary
body: Visit a Bestiary to hire a follower.
This building can be found in the world or built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Jeweller
body: Visit a Jeweller to attach Adornments to your pieces of equipment. Additionally, Jewellers will sell basic Adornments to you.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Residence
body: Residences are built in your Origin Town to increase its population. A higher population will increase your daily login income, and increase the chance that your townspeople will give you a gift at a Citadel.

topics.name: Citadel
body: The Citadel is built in your Origin Town, and allows your townspeople to occasionally provide you with a gift.
These gifts can be pieces of equipments, or consumable items useful to any player.

topics.name: Town Hall
body: The Town Hall is built in your Origin Town. Your townspeople will post quests here for you to complete. Completing quests will increase your town's morale, increase your daily login income, and increase the chance at receiving a gift at a Citadel.

topics.name: Wayvessel
body: You can build a Wayvessel to teleport to other players' Origin Towns. These players must be in your party.
Both Wayvessels must be activated in order to teleport between them.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Appraiser
body: An appraiser can determine the quality rating of newly acquired items.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Grand Market
body: The Grand Market is an upgraded version of the humble shop. It can be upgraded to level 100 and sell many items, however it cannot be shared with other players.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Herbalist
body: The Herbalist allows players to craft potions using empty bottles and materials that they may find in their travels. Its available potion recipes will change every day.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

topics.name: Refinery
body: The Refinery allows players to recycle materials, yielding collections of new materials. Higher rarity of materials will yield better results.
This building can be built in your Origin Town.

events.name: A Feast of Feathers
events.description: Help Justin Beaker prepare a large feast for the townsfolk. If we all band together, Guilds will be more rewarding to us.

help_text.body: In this community event, we help Justin Beaker prepare a large feast for the townsfolk.
for T4+ players, contribute to the Community Quests to collectively earn a bonus to Guild rewards.

events.name: Balor Invades
events.description: The forces of Balor have invaded! Hold them back in this unique event.

events.name: Beastfelled
events.description: Sword or no sword, staff or no staff. To don a suit of armor or leave ourselves vulnerable. Trials await us.

help_text.body: Beastfelled is a unique event that involves completing difficult challenges.
For those looking for an additional challenge, talk to Eriq of Annwn to get started.

For T7+ players, craft the Beastfelled Dungeon Key in the Event Hub or Monumental Guild Hall to unlock the Beastfelled Dungeon. This item will allow you to run any battle dungeon as a Beastfelled Dungeon instead.
For T10+ players, craft the Beastfelled Summoning Scroll in the Event Hub or Monumental Guild Hall to summon the powerful super raid, Turned King Lyncus.

allegiance_unlocks.name: EXP Potion
allegiance_unlocks.description: A sour tasting elixir that doubles experience earned for 1 hour.

allegiance_unlocks.name: Diluted Mnemonic

events.name: Canada D'eh
events.description: Northern Forge is proudly Canadian! Celebrate Canada Day with us in this special event.

help_text.body: For T3+ players, earn Timber the Beaver's Chewed Lumber by completing Dungeons, Monuments, and Raids.
These items can be traded for various rewards at the Monumental Guild Hall during this event.
These items can also be found while exploring the world via the Traveler's Guild.

events.name: EXP Event
events.description: For a limited time, earn 20% more experience from defeating monsters.

events.name: Evercalm: Mental Health Awareness
events.description: Learn about practicing breathing and mindfulness!

help_text.body: In this event, we learn about the importance of breathing and mindfulness. Taking a moment to breathe can help us feel more centered and calm.
For all players, a special breathing exercise can be accessed from the Oracle Temple.
We encourage you to take a few moments each day to practice mindful breathing.

events.name: Fool of April
events.description: Once a Fool, twice a Fool, thrice a Fool he was. Always a Fool, never a Fool, if only he knew of combat.

help_text.body: The Fool of April is here. Join your Kingdom against this silly Raid to earn rewards found elsewhere throughout the year.
For T8+ players, look for curious monsters in Dungeons or the World to find Playing Cards, exchangeable for rewards in the Event Hub.

events.name: Giant Steps
events.description: For a limited time, your steps will awaken Traveler Aspects much faster.

help_text.body: During Giant Steps, each step you take in the real world will transfer to additional in-game steps. This will charge your Aspects much faster.

events.name: Golden Week
events.description: It's Golden Week! Enjoy triple the gold from defeating enemies. Additionally, quests will give 25% more rewards.

help_text.body: During Golden Week, all players will earn triple the gold from defeating enemies. Additionally, quests will give 25% more rewards.

events.name: Great Felling
events.description: For a limited time, earn extra experience, gold, orns, and items from defeating Raids.

events.name: Kingsfall
events.subtitle: Remembering the Fallen
events.description: Avalon, rich of heroes, beasts, and lore cannot be forgotten. Challenge its fallen heroes and collect its legendary beasts in this event!

help_text.body: In Kingsfall, we learn more about the great kingdom of Avalon and its fallen heroes.
For T6+ players, talk to Guinevere to begin the Kingsfall questline.
For T6+ players, craft Vials of Lakewater in the Event Hub or Monumental Guild to enter the Nimue's Lake and challenge the fallen knights of Arthus.
For T8+ players, craft the Broceliande Candle to gain exclusive Steward followers of Avalon.
For T10+ players, craft Hippogriff Summoning Scrolls or Crest of a Fallen King to summon this event's super raids.
During Kingsfall, you will be able to equip one additional Traveler's Guild Aspect at a time. Additionally, rewards from the Traveler's Guild will be increased.

events.name: Laborlight
events.description: A celebration of the land's Artisans, Laborlight is here.

help_text.body: In Laborlight, we celebrate the proud Artisans of the land.
Talk to Dudley for a quick questline as he tries to forge a hammer of ages.
Throughout the duration of Laborlight, all blacksmith gear upgrades will take 25% less materials.

events.name: Lucky Event
events.description: For a limited time, items have an extra 50% chance of dropping from monsters.

events.name: Lunar Festival
events.description: Celebrate the Lunar Festival with increased Proof drops from all Guilds.

events.name: Menders of Hearts
events.description: Spread the love in this event featuring love and love lost.

help_text.body: In Menders of Hearts, we encounter the exiled Elysian God Anteros and his followers.
Anteros was banished from the lands for his pursuit of the destruction of love.

For T3+ players, encounter the followers of Anteros in Dungeons to collect their Broken Hearts. These Broken Hearts can be mended in the Event Hub, granting the Lover's Bonus effect. This effect slightly increases the quality that items may drop at.
Crafting the Lover's Bonus will also increase a 'Heartmender' profile badge.
For T10+ players, encounter Anteros and his guards in Towers of Olympia.

events.name: Of Giants and Titans
events.subtitle: The Great Space Race
events.description: Learn about Jotunheim and Olympia's race to the skies in this limited storyline!

help_text.body: In "Of Giants and Titans", we meet Kaari of Jotunheim  to learn the story of the Jotunheim Giants and the Olympian Titans.
For T4+ players, earn Fragments of Olympic Memories from Memory Hunts. This item can be used to craft a Mnemosyne Mnemonic at the Monumental Guild, giving access to a unique Tower of Olympia.
For T6+ players, find Jotunheim's fallen warriors in Dungeons to collect Celestial Stardrops. Celestial Stardrops can be used to summon apparitions of Giants of the past.
For T8+ players, find Jotunheim's fallen warriors in Dungeons to additionally collect Celestial Moondrops. Celestial Moondrops can be used to summon apparitions of Titans of the past.

For T9+ players, earn additional Fragments of Olympic Memories by completing Towers of Olympia. This item can be used to craft a Mnemosyne Puzzle Key at the Monumental Guild, giving access to the "Shadows of the Titans" Tower of Olympia mode.
For T10+ players, craft the "Tablet of Hyperion" at the Monumental Guild to challenge the super raid Hyperion.

events.name: Ornaversary!

events.subtitle: From the ashes, who will rise?
events.description: Phoenixrise has returned. Help Asherah in her undying pledge to stop the ritual of old.

help_text.body: Phoenixrise has returned: an event about a shared mission to stop an ancient ritual.
For Tier 2+ players, talk to Asherah to learn more about the ritual and what we can do to stop it.
When the player community is successful in stopping the ritual, Phoenixrise's Community Quest will reward everyone.

events.name: Ragnarok
events.description: Stop Ragnarok by defeating the southern wanderers of Nothren.

help_text.body: In Ragnarok, we meet a curious "Nothren Lorekeeper" who guides us through stories of old Nothren Lords.

For Tier 4+ players, find the "Seedhusk of Yggdrasil" dungeons scattered throughout the world. These dungeons include a unique challenge that awards the Seed of Yggdrasil, which can be exchanged in the Event Hub for various rewards.

For Tier 5+ players, earn the Runes of Huginn and Muninn by defeating the Nothren Lords as Raids, or by completing dungeons. These runes can be used to craft event scrolls or purchase various rewards in the Event Hub.

For Tier 7+ players, construct Scrolls of Ragnarok or Yggdrasil in the Event Hub from Runes of Huginn, Runes of Muninn, and Seeds of Yggdrasil. These scrolls can be used to summon the powerful Jormungandr or Yggdrasil super raids.

events.description: In this event, earn 25% more orns from defeating monsters. Dungeons can also be entered more frequently.

events.name: Stop Scruug!
events.description: Stop Scruug from ruining the holiday season!

events.name: Sumner Games
events.description: Compete for glory in the Sumner Games!

help_text.body: In the Sumner Games, we encounter twelve old Gods of Olympia.

Once upon a time, these Gods participated in great games for the enjoyment of the people. However, when the Olympians turned their attention on building great towers, these games were lost. What a shame!
For Tier 5+ players, find one of four Old Olympian Gods in the World to receive their Bronze Medals.
For Tier 7+ players, find one of four Old Olympian Gods in the Dungeons to receive their Silver Medals.
For Tier 9+ players, find one of four Old Olympian Gods in the Towers of Olympia to receive their Gold Medals.
Trade these medals at the Monumental Guild for unique sprites and a Citadel theme, taking on their appearance and reliving their legacy!

events.name: Surrounded by Memories
events.description: For a limited time, earn additional experience, gold, and orns when completing Shattered Memory Hunts.

events.name: Terra's Day
events.description: Join us this Earth Week as we meet Gi and learn of the fate of Terra.

help_text.body: Gloom, Murk, and Grisal. These are the themes of the Terra events.
Join us for Gi's storyline, one the tells us of the fate of Terra.
Please see the "Terra's Legacy" tab of the Event Hub to interact with this event.

events.name: Terra's Legacy
events.description: Gi of Terra has a new story for us. Let's learn more of the fate of Terra.

help_text.body: Gloom, Murk, and Grisal. These are the themes of the Terra events.
Join us for Gi's enhanced storyline, one the tells us of the fate of Terra.
Please see the "Terra's Legacy" tab of the Event Hub to interact with this event.

events.name: Terra's Legacy: Natureblight
events.description: Fight with nature against the scourge of Murk.

help_text.body: The people of Terra neglected their planet's natural resources for decades, using approximately 1.6 Terras worth of resources per year. When the Murk and Gloom came, the Nature of Terra was too weak to fight back. Many already endangered species were lost in a moment.
In Terra's Legacy: Natureblight, we fight alongside our endangered friends against the Murk.

events.name: Terra's Legacy: Rainsong
events.description: Learn more about Terra's fate and the Final Bloom in this instalment of Terra's Legacy.

help_text.body: In Terra's Legacy: Rainsong, we aim to stop the Final Bloom together.
For T3+ players, travel to the Congo to enter the Final Bloom Lair dungeon, but only when we have all defeated enough of the Final Bloom together.
Similarly, for T7+ players, travel to Maluku Island to enter the Monument of the Murk.
Finally, for T10+ players, travel to the Amazon to take on the Rainforest Destroyer Murk.

events.name: The Crimson Festival
events.subtitle: The crimson flowers grow
events.description: It is time for the Crimson Festival! Paint the world Crimson alongside the people of Lerna.

help_text.body: For T4+ players, talk to Ariadne to begin the Crimson Festival questline, learning of the Crimson Festival of Lerna.
During the Crimson Festival, receive Proofs of Crimson by completing Dungeons, defeating Raids, or winning in the Blades of Finesse.
For T6+ players, craft the Crimson Summoning Scrolls in the Event Hub using the essences of Cerus, Aries, and Perseus.
The Scroll of Crimson Chaos can be crafted and used during this event only. Use it to encounter additional event monsters in the world.
For T10+ players, craft the Lerna Summoning Scroll in the Event Hub to summon the super raid, Fallen King Centaurus.

events.name: The Cursed Queens
events.subtitle: Ulster and the Sisters of Morrigan
events.description: Learn more of The Morrigan and challenge her sisters, creations, and Arisen self in this event.

help_text.body: In The Cursed Queens, we encounter both Morrigan's sisters and her creations as we complete a questline to learn her backstory and the fate of King Ulster.
For T6, T7, and T8+ players, challenge Morrigan's sisters Badb, Macha, and Neman as both Kingdom and World Raids.
For T7+ players, encounter the Fey creations of Morrigan to earn the Caoranach's Lair Key, allowing you to run any dungeon as a Caoranach's Lair.
For T10+ players, defeat Caoranach in his lair to earn the Oillipheist Tower Key, allowing you to run any Tower of Olympia as a Tower of Oillipheist.
For T10+ players, challenge Arisen Morrigan for some of the most powerful rewards in the game.

events.subtitle: Trick or Treat, Trick or Treat!
events.description: Until we say farewell to the Hallowed, enjoy double the Treats when Trick or Treating at Haunted Houses.

help_text.body: In The Hallowed, we meet Feralia, a guide to a very strange story about a certain oranged-headed being.
Trick or Treat at Haunted Houses to earn double the Treats for your Loot Bag.
For T5+ players, join a scavenger hunt for monsters carrying a certain pumpkin pail within the World, Dungeons, Monuments, and Towers.
For T8+ players, craft the Hallowed Summoning Scroll at the Monumental Guild with the materials found from these curious monsters. This item will summon the powerful Pumpkinless super raid.
For T10+ players, the Arisen Hallowed Summoning Scroll is available at the Monumental Guild.

events.name: The Mimics Are Loose
events.subtitle: Is that a treasure chest?!
events.description: The Mimics are here to spread their mischief and chaos! Fight them in both World Raids and Kingdom Raids in this event.

help_text.body: The Mimics are loose! The Mimics are loose!
Join your Kingdom or party mates to take on these...interesting...Raids to earn a great variety of rewards usually seen elsewhere throughout the year.

events.name: The Mischievous Clurichauns
events.description: The fairies of Naggeneen have shown themselves! End their mischief in raids and dungeons to earn unique rewards! Additionally, you will receive extra gold from defeating any enemy.

events.name: The Plight of Apollyon
events.subtitle: Once a Hero, now a Villain
events.description: In this event, we recall the terrible plight of the Balor Mystic, Apollyon. Once a hero -- now a villain!

help_text.body: In the Plight of Apollyon, we encounter shattered memories of Apollyon and his pupils' past. During this event, Memory Hunts will be more rewarding.

For T3+ players, Amities with effects unique to this event only can be found in the "Rewards" tab of the Event Hub. These Amities will cost Balor Memories, found by defeating the pupils of Apollyon. These Amities will refresh each day.
For T3+ players, find the memories of Apollyon's students in Dungeons and Monuments.
For T6+ players, fight a memory of Apollyon in both Kingdom and World Raids.
For Tier 10+ players, craft the Balor Mnemonic in the Event Hub or Monumental Guild to transport yourself to Apollyon's Distorted Memory.

events.subtitle: Makers of Kingdoms, Makers of Thrones
events.description: Explore the origins of the great Kingdoms in this unique questline.

help_text.body: In Thronemakers, we learn the true origin stories of the great Kingdoms of these lands.
For T4+ players, speak with the Aaru Storyteller to begin Thronemakers questline.
For T6+ players, encounter Shades of the great Thronemakers in Monuments to earn Old Aaru Seals.
For T7+ players, challenge the Thronemakers in their Raid form to earn Old Aaru Seals.
For T10+ players, craft the Scroll of Dynasty at the Monumental Guild to challenge the powerful super raid, The Great Sphinx.

events.subtitle: Don't forget your Codex!
events.description: Long ago, this land was created by the Great Dragons. Twice a year, they return to see it.

help_text.body: In Wyrmhunt, we meet the Great Dragons of old.
For Tier 5+ players, meet with Dragonhunter Brin to begin a great hunt of Dragons.
Additionally, these Great Dragons will be available to you in the Event Hub when their Codex entries have been completed.

For endgame players looking for a deeper challenge, craft the Yelbeghen Tower Key at the Monumental Guild with heads found when defeating the Great Dragons. This item will allow you to run any Tower of Olympia as a Tower of Yelbeghen instead.

classlines.label: Valor
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Warrior
classlines.description: Warriors and Knights of Lyonesse wield traditional weapons, wear heavy armor, and enter battle using less advanced techniques. They prioritize survivability in battle and learn simple in-battle abilities.

classlines.label: Omnimancy
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Mage
classlines.description: Avalon is known for its deep understading of the magical arts. Mages of Avalon prioritize casting powerful spells in combat. They must prioritize balancing the recovery of both mana and HP in battle.

classlines.label: Shadowmancy
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Thief
classlines.description: Annwn is a ancient Kingdom known for its adept nature in the clandestine arts. Thieves of Annwn are quick on their feet and prioritize speed, debuffs, and critical hits in combat. They will have less defenses than other classes and may be found to be more difficult to play.

classlines.label: Valhallan
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Tamer
classlines.description: Tamers of Nothren are known for their ability to tame and control beasts. They prioritize utilizing their followers' abilities in battle. These may be found to be more difficult to play.

classlines.label: Elysian
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Summoner
classlines.description: The Elysian summoners use ancient techniques to summon beasts in battle to fight on their behalf. They prioritize survivability in battle and are found to be the easiest to play.

classlines.label: The Old Gods
classlines.subtitle: Path of the Gods
classlines.description: When one has become powerful enough, we may channel the powers of the Old Gods.

classlines.label: The Elderred
classlines.subtitle: What once was
classlines.description: The Elderred are classes that you have unlocked in the past, but are no longer available to new players.
